items.gist: The external upāya is examined: three kinds of place (prāṇa, body, outside) and eleven external ritual objects.
The whole sixfold adhva is established in prāṇa; krama and akrama are the play of Kālī, the supreme Śakti.
Pure consciousness becomes prāṇa-spanda, animating the body; the deluded mistake bodily activity for all reality.
When one vāsanā weakens, another may arise, including the especially sinful nāstikya vāsanā.
The adhva is divided by action and form; the śikhā, time, bindu, and related powers are established in prāṇa.
The adhva is the appearance of form and action in consciousness, the means of reaching the goal.
The terms for adhva are explained: kāla-adhva and deśa-adhva, each with three levels, making six.
The kāla adhva unfolds tattvas from Śiva down to prāṇa, body, and the unity of knower and known.
Prāṇa pervades the body but is not fully manifest; its paths and nāḍīs are described.
Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī are the three Śaktis governing prāṇa and effort in different beings.
Without knowing creation, maintenance, and dissolution one is not liberated; all these are time-bound and prāṇa-based, hence utterance.
